subject: Dedicated GPU workshop: sizing, traffic profile, and next steps
messages:
From: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@brightretail.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T15:12:00Z
Subject: Request: Workshop to validate Dedicated GPU sizing for BrightRetail

Hi Markus,

Thanks for the intro, Marissa. Were preparing to move a substantial part of BrightRetails inference traffic to a dedicated pool and want to validate sizing assumptions before the procurement cycle. High level:

- Peak QPS currently ~220 requests/sec with strong spikiness around 2pm PST.
- Average prompt length ~350 tokens, average response ~420 tokens, some long replies up to ~1,800 tokens for rich product descriptions.
- Concurrency distribution is heavy-tailed: 60% of requests are <2s, 10% end up >6s because of long responses and reranking steps.

Wed like to run a 60–90 minute workshop next week to:
1) walk you through our traffic patterns and sample prompts (attached sample CSV),
2) validate batching/latency SLO tradeoffs, and
3) surface fallback policies for peak days.

Attached is a small traffic sample and a short agenda. Can you send a short template with the sizing inputs youd like filled out prior to the call (concurrency buckets, target P99 latency, tolerance for quantization)?

Thanks,
Alex

--
Alex Zhou
Head of Applied ML, BrightRetail
alex.zhou@brightretail.com
(415) 555-0123

Attachments: brightretail_traffic_sample.csv, workshop_agenda-v1.pdf

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@brightretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Workshop to validate Dedicated GPU sizing for BrightRetail

Alex thanks for the context and sample. Available for a workshop — suggested goals below and a short prework template attached (redwood_gpu_sizing_template.xlsx).

Proposed workshop goals:
- Confirm realistic steady-state qps vs. burst requirements (including monthly peak days).
- Map prompt/response size distribution to batching strategy and expected GPU utilization.
- Produce a first-pass dedicated fleet recommendation with margin assumptions and SLA options.

Prework items (can be high-level):
- 7-day qps/time-of-day by 5-minute bins (sample okay).
- Histogram of prompt tokens and response tokens (percentiles).
- A small set (~10) of representative prompts and an example long-response case.

We can run through a live sizing exercise during the call; Dev will have the fleet-sizing model handy. When are you free for a 60 minute slot next week? Im proposing:
- Tue Nov 2, 10:00–11:00 PT
- Wed Nov 3, 13:00–14:00 PT

If you prefer, we can do a 90 min session and include a quick canary rollout plan.

Thanks,
Markus

--
Markus Klein
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_gpu_sizing_template.xlsx

From: Alex Zhou <alex.zhou@brightretail.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T16:21:00Z
Subject: Re: Request: Workshop to validate Dedicated GPU sizing for BrightRetail

Markus,

Tue Nov 2 at 10:00 PT works for us — Ive filled out the template and attached a slightly larger traffic sample (brightretail_traffic_sample.csv). Quick clarifications up front so we dont waste time on the call:

- P99 latency target for interactive flows: 450ms. For batch/reranking flows were ok with higher P99s (2.5s).
- Tolerance for slight quality degradation from int8 quantization is acceptable for >95% of traffic; the long narrative generation must remain fp16.
- Well want a canary rollout path and a plan for autoscaling + burst credit handling during promotional campaigns.

Looking forward to the session. Please send a calendar invite and any reading youd like us to do in advance.

Best,
Alex

--
Alex Zhou
Head of Applied ML, BrightRetail

Attachments: brightretail_traffic_sample.csv (v2)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
